terms.gloss: a wave, a billow, above all of the sea
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.16.6: flūctum ā saxō frangī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 5.5: ad flūctum ajunt dēclāmāre solitum Dēmosthenem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From fluō; most often in the plural.

phrases.english: Do you want big waves or little waves?

phrases.latin: ad flūctum ajunt dēclāmāre solitum Dēmosthenem, ut fremitum assuēsceret vōce vincere
phrases.english: they say Demosthenes used to declaim to the waves, to accustom himself to mastering a roar with his voice

phrases.latin: Hodiē flūctūs magnī sunt; prope lītus manē.
phrases.english: The waves are big today; stay near the shore.

phrases.latin: nōndum erat tempestās, sed jam inclīnātiō maris ac subinde crēbrior flūctus
phrases.english: there was no storm yet, but the sea was already heaving, and the waves came more and more often

phrases.latin: sī quandō Āfricō mare impulsum est, frāctīs jam et novissimīs flūctibus leviter alluitur
phrases.english: whenever the sea is driven by the south-west wind, (the dining room) is lightly washed by the last spent waves
